Rashi on Gittin 54a:10:1.hebrew: ואמר רב אחא בריה דרב איקא - ביבמות בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צ.): דמזיד נמי, דקאמר ר' מאיר "אין תשלומיו תשלומין", להפטר לגמרי קאמר — כלומר, שצריך לחזור ולשלם חולין טהורין כרבנן — ובשוגג הוא דפליג אדרבנן, דלרבי מאיר לא קנסו שוגג אטו מזיד, ורבנן קנסו. והא הכא איסורא דרבנן היא, דמדאורייתא תשלומין מעליא נינהו, דלפי מדה משלם; וכי משלם טמאין אפי' במזיד, איסורא דרבנן הוא דעבד, ולא קניס רבי מאיר שוגג:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:10:1.english: And Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said - in Yevamot, in [the chapter] Ha'isha Rabbah (Yevamot 90a): [He explains] that regarding an intentional [offender] as well, when Rabbi Meir says "his payment is not [a valid] payment," he means [as far as] being completely exempt — that is to say, he must go back and pay [with] pure non-sacred [produce], like the Rabbis [hold] — and it is regarding an unintentional [offender] that he disagrees with the Rabbis, for according to Rabbi Meir they did not penalize an unintentional [offender] on account of an intentional [offender], whereas the Rabbis did penalize [him]. And here, it is a rabbinic prohibition, for by Torah law it is a valid payment, since one pays by measure; and when one pays [with] impure [produce], even intentionally, it is a rabbinic prohibition that he has transgressed, and Rabbi Meir does not penalize an unintentional [offender]:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:11:1.english: He intends to pay - and he is an upright person:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:11:2.hebrew: ואנן ניקום ונקנסיה - על שגגתו, אבל מטמא ומדמע שוגג, אינו מתעסק בטובה:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:11:2.english: And should we arise and penalize him - for his unwitting error? However, one who unintentionally renders [produce] impure or mixes [terumah with ordinary produce] is not engaged in a beneficial [act]:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:12:1.english: Unintentionally, it is accepted - For the tzitz [the High Priest's frontlet] effects acceptance, and the meat is permitted to be eaten:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:12:2.hebrew: במזיד לא הורצה - מדרבנן, וקנסא הוא לאסור בשר באכילה, אבל בעלים נתכפרו. והך זריקת מזיד איסורא דרבנן היא, דמדאורייתא זורק לכתחילה, דהציץ מרצה:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:12:2.english: [If he sprinkled it] intentionally, it is not accepted - [This is] by rabbinic law, and it is a penalty to forbid the meat from being eaten, though the owners have achieved atonement. And this intentional sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition, for by Torah law one may sprinkle [it] in the first place, since the tzitz [the High Priest's headplate] effects acceptance:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:13:1.hebrew: ואנן ניקום ונקנסיה - על שגגתו. וה"ה דמצי לשנויי: הא מני? רבי יהודה היא, דלא קניס בדרבנן, דהא לאו סתם משנה היא, אלא ברייתא היא במנחות בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כה.); מיהו ניחא ליה לשנויי דאפי' תימא רבי מאיר היא:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:13:1.english: And should we arise and penalize him - for his unwitting [act]. And it could just as well have answered: Whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Yehudah['s], who does not penalize in rabbinic [matters] — for this is not an anonymous Mishnah, but rather a Baraita in Menachot, in [the chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 25a); however, it prefers to answer [in a way] that even if you say it is Rabbi Meir['s view]:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:14:1.hebrew: המעשר בשבת - איסור שבות דרבנן היא, כדתנן במשילין (ביצה דף לו.): "אלו הן משום שבות של מצוה: אין מגביהין תרומות ומעשרות", דמיחזי כמתקן. והך "המעשר בשבת", סתם משנה היא במסכת תרומות (פ"ב מ"ג). וכן "המטביל כליו" — מטביל נמי איסורא דרבנן היא, במסכת ביצה בפרק י"ט (דף יח.), מפני שנראה כמתקן כלי. וכל הני רמינן דרבי מאיר אדרבי מאיר, דקניס לעיל בדרבנן:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:14:1.english: One who tithes on Shabbat - It is a rabbinic prohibition of shevut [activity prohibited on Shabbat by rabbinic decree], as we learned in a mishnah in [the chapter entitled] Mashilin (Beitzah 36a): "These are [prohibited] on account of shevut [and] of a mitzvah: one may not separate terumot and tithes," because it appears as though one is repairing [the produce]. And this [mishnah of] "One who tithes on Shabbat" is an anonymous mishnah in Tractate Terumot (2:3). And similarly, "one who immerses his vessels" — immersing [vessels] is also a rabbinic prohibition, [as taught] in Tractate Beitzah in the chapter [entitled] Yom Tov (18a), because it appears as though one is repairing a vessel. And all of these we raise as a contradiction of Rabbi Meir against Rabbi Meir, who penalized above regarding a rabbinic [prohibition]:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:1:1.hebrew: ואין מונין - נטיעותיהן לשבתות, שאין מונין ימים לנטיעה אלא שנים, לפיכך אין הדבר ידוע לזמן מרובה שנטע בשבת:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:1:1.english: And they do not count - their saplings by Shabbats [i.e., weeks], for one does not count days for a sapling, only years; therefore, after a long time it is not known that he planted [it] on Shabbat:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:3:1.english: What [is the point of] "alternatively" - Why did he need to bring another reason?

Rashi on Gittin 54a:3:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר וכי תימא שבתות נמי - זימנין דצריך למימני, דתניא: הנוטע ערב שביעית ל' יום לפני ראש השנה, עלתה לו שנה לשני ערלה — דשלשים יום בשנה חשובין שנה — ומותר לקיימן בשביעית; פחות משלשים יום לפני ראש השנה, לא עלתה לו שנה, ואסור לקיימן בשביעית; הלכך, זמנין דשבת זו שנטע זה הויא יום שלשים לפני ר"ה, ומונין אותו שנה, ואי הוה בציר ההוא יומא לא הוה סליק ליה שתא; ולאחר זמן, כשאוכלין מן הפירות לסוף שתי שנים, ואומרים: "למה הותרו פירות הללו לשתי שנים?", ואומר להם: "השלשים שלפני ר"ה חשובין שנה", ומזכירים שנטע בשבת — וליקנסוה:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:3:2.english: This is what [Rabbi Meir] is saying: And if you would say [people count] Sabbaths as well - [meaning] sometimes one needs to count [from Shabbat], as it was taught [in a baraita]: If one plants [a tree] on the eve of the Sabbatical year thirty days before Rosh Hashanah, it counts for him as a year toward the years of orlah — for thirty days in a year are considered a [full] year — and it is permitted to keep them [the saplings] during the Sabbatical year; [if planted] less than thirty days before Rosh Hashanah, it does not count for him as a year, and it is forbidden to keep them during the Sabbatical year. Therefore, sometimes this Shabbat on which this [person] planted is the thirtieth day before Rosh Hashanah, and they count it as a year, whereas if that day had been lacking, it would not have counted for him as a year; and after some time, when they eat from the fruits at the end of two years, and they say, "Why were these fruits permitted after two years?" and he says to them, "The thirty [days] before Rosh Hashanah are considered a year," they will remember that he planted [it] on Shabbat — so let them penalize him:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:4:1.hebrew: תא שמע דבר אחר נחשדו ישראל על שביעית - ואיכא למיחש, מתוך שהדבר ניכר, אתי למישרי נטיעה בשביעית:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:4:1.english: Come [and] hear, alternatively: Jews are suspected regarding [the] Sabbatical [Year] - And there is [reason] to be concerned [that] since the matter is noticeable, [people] will come to permit planting in the Sabbatical [Year]:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:4:2.hebrew: ולא נחשדו על שבתות - ואפילו יזכר ויודע הדבר, לא אתי למישרי נטיעתא בשבת:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:4:2.english: And they are not suspected of [desecrating] Shabbat - And even if it is remembered and the matter becomes known, one will not come to permit planting on Shabbat:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:6:1.english: Dayyara bar dayyarta - A convert, son of a female convert:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:1.hebrew: ת"ש - דרבי מאיר בדרבנן לא קניס שוגג:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:1.english: Come and hear - that Rabbi Meir does not penalize an unintentional [transgressor] in [matters of] rabbinic [law]:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:2.english: One partook of teruma - unintentionally, and even [if it was] impure:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:3.hebrew: משלם חולין טהורין - ולקמן פריך: אמאי משלם טהורין? האוכל תרומה שוגג — אינו משלם מעות אלא תבואה, ואינו משלם תרומה אלא חולין מתוקנין, ועל ידי תשלומין הן נעשין תרומה, שנאמר: "ונתן לכהן את הקדש" (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ד) — על ידי נתינתו נעשו קודש; אלמא דבר הראוי לחול עליו שם תרומה בעינן, ולא מעות. אבל האוכלה מזיד — משלם מעות:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:3.english: He pays [with] ritually pure, non-sacred [produce] - And later [the Gemara] asks: Why does he pay [with] pure [produce]? One who eats teruma unintentionally does not pay money, but rather produce, and he does not pay [with] teruma, but rather [with] tithed non-sacred [produce], and through [the act of] payment it becomes teruma, as it is stated: "And he shall give the holy thing to the priest" (Leviticus 22:14) — through his giving, it becomes holy. Thus, we require something fit for the designation of teruma to take effect upon it, and not money. However, one who eats it intentionally pays money:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:4.hebrew: בשוגג - אם בשוגג שילם, שלא היה יודע שהן טמאין:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:4.english: Unintentionally - If he paid unintentionally, [meaning] that he did not know that they were [ritually] impure:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:5.hebrew: תשלומיו תשלומין - ופטור באלו, והן נעשין תרומה טמאה כמה שאכל:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:5.english: His payment is [a valid] payment - And he is exempt [from further payment] with these [impure non-sacred produce], and they become impure terumah, like what he ate:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:6.english: Intentionally, his payment is not [a valid] payment - and later [the Gemara] asks: why?

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:7.english: Both this and that - [whether] unintentional or intentional:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:8.hebrew: תשלומיו תשלומין - והן נעשין תרומה וממון כהן, ואם קידש בהן אשה, מקודשת:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:8.english: His payment is valid - And they become teruma and the property of a priest, and if he betrothed a woman with them, she is betrothed:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:9.hebrew: וחוזר ומשלם חולין טהורים - משום קנס, ואינן נעשין תרומה:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:7:9.english: And he returns and pays [ritually] pure, non-sacred produce - [This is] because of a penalty, and it does not become teruma:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:8:1.hebrew: והוינן בה במזיד אמאי אין תשלומיו תשלומין - אמאי קנסת ליה אמזיד דהני תשלומין? הא לא הזיד בתשלומין גרועין:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:8:1.english: And we discussed it: [If he did so] intentionally, why is his payment not a [valid] payment - Why did you penalize him for [acting] intentionally in this payment? For he did not act intentionally with an inferior payment:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:8:2.hebrew: דאכל מיניה - תרומה טמאה, דלא מצי למיכל בימי טומאה, דהאוכל תרומה בטומאת הגוף במיתה, ואפילו היא טמאה:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:8:2.english: As he ate from him - [i.e., he ate] impure terumah, which [the priest] cannot eat during [his] days of impurity, for one who eats terumah while his body is impure is [liable to] death [at the hand of Heaven], even if it [the terumah] is impure:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:8:3.hebrew: וקמשלם ליה - חולין טמאים דחזו ליה בימי טומאה, ואע"ג דסוף סוף הן נעשין תרומה ולא חזו ליה, דהא טמאה היא, מיהו חולין טמאין מיכוין לשלומי, ולא ידע דהם נעשין תרומה:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:8:3.english: And he pays him - [with] impure non-sacred produce, which is fit for him during [his] days of impurity. And even though in the end it becomes terumah and is not fit for him, since it is impure, nevertheless he intends to pay [with] impure non-sacred produce, and he does not know that it becomes terumah:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:9:1.hebrew: משלם כל דהו - כל שהוא חולין, בין טהורין בין טמאין:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:9:1.english: He pays [with] anything - any non-sacred [produce], whether [ritually] pure or [ritually] impure:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:9:2.hebrew: בשוגג תשלומיו תשלומין - דהא אוכל תרומה שוגג לפי מדה משלם ולא לפי דמים, ואע"ג דהך טומאה גריעא מההיא דאכל — תשלומין הן מדאורייתא, ורבנן נמי לא קנסוהו הואיל ושגג בתשלומין:
Rashi on Gittin 54a:9:2.english: Unintentionally, his payment is valid - For one who partakes of teruma unintentionally pays according to measure and not according to monetary value, and even though this impure [produce] is inferior to that [pure teruma] which he ate, it is [nevertheless] a valid payment by Torah law; and the Rabbis also did not penalize him, since he acted unintentionally in [making] the payment:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:9:3.english: Intentionally - [meaning] that he knew they were [ritually] impure:

Rashi on Gittin 54a:9:4.english: His payment is not valid - because the Rabbis penalized him, since he intended to cause a priest a loss:

Tosafot on Gittin 54a:10:1.hebrew: הכא בקנסו שוגג אטו מזיד כו' - בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צ.), מעיקרא ס"ד דאין תשלומיו תשלומין כלל קא"ר מאיר, ופריך מינה למאן דאמר אין כח ביד חכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה; ומסיק דאין תשלומיו תשלומין וחוזר ומשלם חולין טהורים כדרבנן, ולא פליגי אלא בקנסו שוגג אטו מזיד כו':
Tosafot on Gittin 54a:10:1.english: Here, [the practical difference between them] is whether they penalized an unintentional [offender] due to an intentional [offender], etc. - In [the chapter] HaIsha Rabbah (Yevamot 90a), [the Gemara] initially thought that Rabbi Meir was saying that his payment is not a valid payment at all, and it raises a difficulty from this against the one who says that the Sages do not have the power to uproot a matter from the Torah; and it concludes that [his meaning is that] his payment is not a valid payment and he must go back and pay pure non-sacred produce according to rabbinic law, and they only disagree regarding whether they penalized an unintentional [offender] due to an intentional [offender], etc.:

Tosafot on Gittin 54a:12:1.hebrew: דם שנטמא וזרקו - וא"ת: מאי קשיא ליה לר"מ, והא לאו סתם מתני' היא, דברייתא היא בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כה.)? וי"ל: דסמיך אסתם מתני' דכיצד צולין (פסחים דף פ:), דתנן: הפסח שנזרק דמו ואח"כ נודע שהוא טמא — הציץ מרצה; ודייק בגמ': טעמא דאח"כ נודע, הא נודע ואח"כ נזרק — לא! ומייתי ברייתא דמפרשא בהדיא. והך קושיא — לרבינא דמפרש [בפ' כיצד צולין] (שם) דשוגג קאי אזריקה; דלרב שילא, דמפרש דקאי אטומאה, לא קשה מידי, דטומאה דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Gittin 54a:12:1.english: Blood that became impure and he sprinkled it - And if you will say: What is the difficulty for Rabbi Meir — is this not an anonymous Mishnah, as it is a baraita in [the chapter entitled] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 25a)? And one can say: [The Gemara] relies on the anonymous Mishnah of [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (Pesachim 80b), where we learned: [In the case of] a Paschal offering whose blood was sprinkled and afterward it became known that it was impure, the frontplate [of the High Priest] effects acceptance; and the Gemara infers: the reason is that afterward it became known, [which implies that] if it became known [first] and afterward it was sprinkled, [it is] not [accepted] — and [the Gemara here] cites a baraita that states [this] explicitly. And this difficulty is according to Ravina, who explains [in the chapter Keitzad Tzolin] (there) that "unintentionally" refers to the sprinkling; for according to Rav Shila, who explains that it refers to the impurity, there is no difficulty at all, since [the prohibition of] impurity is of Torah origin:

Tosafot on Gittin 54a:14:1.hebrew: המעשר בשבת - משנה היא בפרק שני דתרומות (משנה ג), וכן ההיא דהמטביל כלים, ופריך מינייהו משום דסתם משנה ר"מ היא. ותימה, דפריך ברישא מההיא דמעשר, והיא שנויה שם בסוף:
Tosafot on Gittin 54a:14:1.english: One who tithes on Shabbat - It is a Mishnah in the second chapter of Terumot (Mishnah 3), and likewise that [case] of "one who immerses vessels [on Shabbat]"; and [the Gemara] raises an objection from them because an anonymous Mishnah is [the view of] Rabbi Meir. And it is surprising that [the Gemara] raises an objection first from that [case] of tithing, whereas it is taught there at the end:

Tosafot on Gittin 54a:8:1.hebrew: וקמשלם מידי דחזי ליה בימי טומאתו - פירוש: קודם שישלם, אבל לאחר ששילם נעשה תרומה ולא חזי ליה:
Tosafot on Gittin 54a:8:1.english: And he pays something that is fit for him during the days of his impurity - Meaning: before he pays, but after he has paid, it becomes teruma and is not fit for him:

Tosafot on Gittin 54a:9:1.hebrew: אכל תרומה טהורה ושילם חולין טמאין מהו כו' בשוגג תשלומיו תשלומין - לא כמו שפירש בקונטרס דקסבר דלפי מדה משלם, דאפי' את"ל דלפי מדה משלם, לא מיפטר אלא אם כן ישלם שיהו שוין להסיקה כשיעור תרומה טהורה שאכל, דלא גרע מגזלן, כדאמר התם: "כל היכא דמעיקרא שויא ד' ולבסוף שויא זוזא, לא תבעי לך דלפי דמים משלם; כי תיבעי לך, דמעיקרא לא שויא אלא זוזא ולבסוף שויא ד'." מ"מ במזיד אין תשלומיו תשלומין, דאכל מידי דקפצי עליה זבינא, ומשלם מידי דלא קפצי עליה זבינא:
Tosafot on Gittin 54a:9:1.english: If he partook of ritually pure teruma, and he paid [with] ritually impure, non-sacred [produce], what is [the halakha], etc.? [If] unintentionally, his payment is valid - Not as Rashi explained, that [the baraita] holds that one pays according to measure; for even if you say that one pays according to measure, he is not exempted unless he pays [impure, non-sacred produce] that is worth, for burning [as fuel], the value of the pure teruma that he ate, since he is no less [liable] than a robber — as [the Gemara] says there: "Wherever it was originally worth four [zuz] and at the end worth one zuz, you should have no question, for he pays according to value; where should you have a question? Where it was originally worth only one zuz and at the end worth four [zuz]." Nevertheless, when [done] intentionally, his payment is not valid, because he ate something that buyers are eager to buy, and he pays with something that buyers are not eager to buy:
